AI can already cut, caption and format a clip for you. Free GitHub skills teach Claude the editing part in minutes. So why isn't everyone going viral off podcast clips? Because editing was never the hard part. Choosing the moment is. AI does not know which 47 seconds out of a two hour conversation deserve to become the clip. No context. No content intelligence. Here is how you build that layer. Scrape the latest 100 clips from the biggest podcast short form accounts. Steven Bartlett, Chris Williamson, Alex Hormozi, anyone running serious long form volume. Capture views, post date, duration, transcript, text overlay and format. Then scrape their original long form episodes and pull the complete transcripts with timestamps. The timestamps are non negotiable. They are what lets Claude match every clip back to the exact episode and the exact moment it came from. Now you reverse engineer the decision. Why those 47 seconds. Where the clip starts. What context got removed. Whether the payoff moved forward. What spoken hook, text overlay and format they used. And how it performed against that account's normal clips. Run enough of these and the patterns surface. Turn the patterns into a Claude skill that understands how the best podcast teams select and package their clips. Then hand it any new timestamped transcript. It returns the strongest moments, exact timestamps, hook options, text overlays, formats and editing instructions. The editing skill does the easy part. None of this needs new software. The tools exist. The clipping skills exist. The data is public. Nobody is assembling it into an intelligence layer. Impossible to fail does not mean every clip goes viral. It means every clip starts with real evidence, and every result makes the next selection smarter. Build the selection layer first. The edit is the easy bit.

The 4 levels of using AI at work How to use AI at work: there are four levels, and most people never leave level one. Chat. You paste something into ChatGPT or Claude, it answers, you copy it back out. Useful, but you're the delivery guy carrying every answer between your apps by hand. Context. Give it your price list, your process docs and ten emails you wrote so it learns how you sound. Same AI, completely different answers, because now it answers like it works at your company. Connected tools. Out of the box, AI can't open your CRM or read your spreadsheet. Almost every app has a door for other software called an API, and MCP is a standard plug that lets AI walk through those doors. Once it's connected, it sees your contacts, your sheets and your email, and it acts: update, send, create. Updating 2,000 customer records from last month's invoices is two weeks of somebody's life. Connected AI does it in minutes. Run it on ten records first, check them, then let it do the rest. Automations. Level three still needs you to ask. Level four starts on its own: a new lead comes in, an invoice lands, Monday at 8am. A tool like n8n moves the data between your apps, and the AI in the middle does the thinking: reads the email, picks the category, writes the reply. Your business keeps running while you sleep. The whole ladder: chat, context, connected tools, automations. On level three you talk and it does the work. On level four you don't even have to talk. 🤖 RUN AI LOCALLY FOR FREE WITH OLLAMA Want to experiment with AI without sending every prompt to a cloud service? Ollama makes it possible to run supported Large Language Models (LLMs) directly on your own computer. ⚠️ EDUCATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY 🧠 WHAT IS OLLAMA? Ollama is a tool for running AI models locally. Instead of using an online AI website, your computer downloads the model and runs the inference on your own machine. That means you can experiment with local AI for: 💻 Coding 🔐 Cybersecurity learning 📚 Research 📝 Writing 📊 Data analysis 🧪 Local experiments 🤖 AI automation ⚙️ HOW IT WORKS The basic workflow is simple: 1️⃣ Install Ollama on your computer. 2️⃣ Choose a model that your hardware can handle. 3️⃣ Download the model. 4️⃣ Start the model locally. 5️⃣ Interact with it through the terminal or compatible applications. Once the model is downloaded, you can continue using it without needing to send every conversation to a remote AI service. 🔐 WHY CYBERSECURITY PEOPLE SHOULD CARE Local AI can be useful in a security lab for tasks such as: • Explaining Linux commands • Understanding logs • Reviewing code • Learning networking concepts • Creating documentation • Analyzing security concepts • Building local AI-assisted tools • Practicing Python You can also connect local models to development tools and build your own AI-powered workflows. 💻 THE IMPORTANT PART Running an LLM locally doesn't automatically make it private or completely secure. Your computer still needs proper security. Keep your operating system updated, protect sensitive files, restrict application permissions, and don't assume that “local” means “risk-free.” 🚀 WHY THIS IS INTERESTING Cloud AI gives you access to powerful models through the internet. Local AI gives you another option: Your hardware → Your model → Your data → Your workflow. The more you understand both approaches, the better you can design secure AI systems. 🔐 HACKWITHBANKS Learn • Build • Test • Defend • Stay Ahead. #Ollama #LocalAI #AI #LLM #ArtificialIntelligence
